placement scarcity: 1 minus min(remaining feasible placements / number of visibility periods of the request, 1). notebooks/03_fixed_bee/03_fixed_threshold_bee.ipynb, cell 41, line 111

mission unmet ratio: 1 minus (seconds allocated so far to the request's mission / seconds requested by that mission this week); not clipped before use. notebooks/03_fixed_bee/03_fixed_threshold_bee.ipynb, cell 41, line 117

placement scarcity: 1 minus (current number of feasible placement candidates / number of candidates when the request was first seen this episode), clipped to [0, 1]. notebooks/04_adaptive_bee/src/bee_fixed_environment.py, line 123

resource contention: dynamic: number of other currently valid requests that share at least one candidate antenna, divided by (number of valid requests - 1), capped at 1 (normalisation: none beyond the division by (valid requests - 1); recomputed at every step). notebooks/04_adaptive_bee/src/bee_fixed_environment.py, line 107

mission unmet ratio: 1 minus (seconds allocated so far to the request's mission / seconds requested by that mission this week), clipped to [0, 1]. notebooks/04_adaptive_bee/src/bee_fixed_environment.py, line 129
contention increase: max(current contention - contention when the request was first seen this episode, 0). notebooks/04_adaptive_bee/src/bee_adaptive_environment.py, line 105

Beams link a DSN complex to a spacecraft while one of its requests is being served. An array draws one beam per complex it uses (for example DSS-34_DSS-35 draws one beam from Canberra; DSS-25_DSS-34 draws one from Goldstone and one from Canberra).

Spacecraft positions are illustrative. Times, antennas, missions and which requests were scheduled are real data. Earth’s rotation follows the schedule time; the lighting is only there to make the globe readable.
Unscheduled requests are listed on the right; they never draw a beam.
Compare mode shows two methods on the same week and seeds, and marks requests that only one of them scheduled.
Every number comes from the team's result files through the export script. Missing data shows as pending.
Averages are taken over evaluation seeds, then training seeds, then the five test weeks (folds).
Differences are written as “higher” or “lower by X” and always shown next to a scale: the seed-to-seed spread on W50, or n = 5 folds.
